To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have confirmed ZnT8 as one of the major targets for autoantibody reactivity in our Danish type 1 diabetes cohort, and that the relationship between auto-antibody specificity to the ZnT8 isoforms, rs13266634, AAD, and HbA1C is dependent on the HLA-DQ genotype of the individual.

the ZnT8 autoantibody (ZnTAA) specificity for the Zn8 Arg325Trptophan epitope is correlated with rs13266634 genotype, and that ZnT8R is associated with HLA DQB1*0301/02 and a lower prevalence of ZnT8R in patients with an early age of diagnosis.

the correlation between the rs13266634 variant and autoantibody specificities for the ZnT 8 Arg325Trptryptophan epitopes is independent of autoantibody titres and that the rs13266635 variant affects autoantibody prevalence and titres for the ZnT-8 Arg325Trppositive autoantibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ZnT8 autoantibodies in type 1 diabetes, with particular focus on the correlation between auto-antibody specificity, rs13266634 genotype and HLA-DQ.
the genetic and immunological basis of type 1 diabetes, and the aim of our study is to identify genetic and immunological factors that contribute to the development of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

the genetic, environmental and immunological factors that lead to type 1 diabetes, and we are currently investigating the relationship between autoimmunity, genetic factors and metabolic control in type 1 diabetes in the Danish population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ZnT8A and rs1326663 genotype are not related to the residual β-cell function in newly diagnosed T1D.

the ZnT8R epitope is more prevalent in patients carrying the T2D associated risk allele rs13266634, and that the ZnT 8R epitope may be a more specific marker of autoantibody development in patients with an earlier onset of diabetes.
the ZnT8A specificity is associated with the rs13266634 genotype and the AAD, but not with HLA-DQ or measures of β-cell functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ZnT8A is a strong predictor for the rs13266634 genotype, but the rs13266633 genotype is a poor predictor for ZnT8 autoantibody status.
ZnT8 autoantibodies are associated with the ZnT8R isoform in probands with rs13266634 genotype, and that ZnT8R autoantibodies may be associated with HLA-DQ3.2.
ZnT8A are a major target at T1D onset in children and adolescents and that the correlation between ZnTT8A and rs13266633 genotypes is not related to residual β-cell function at disease onset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rs13266634 genotype is associated with ZnT8A specificity in a manner that is dependent on autoantibody status for GADA, IA-2A or HLA-DQB genotype.
the correlation between rs13366634 genotype and autoantibody reactivity against the ZnT8R isoforms is present in our Danish cohort of newly diagnosed T1D patients.

autoantibodies targeting the ZnT8 protein are a major component of the autoantibody repertoire at the time of T1D diagnosis and that the rs13266634 genotype affects the specificity of these autoantibodies in a similar fashion as previously shown for autoantibody targeting GAD and IA-2.
